tagging_rule: Every wrong single_best option and every numeric_entry common_error must carry exactly one misconception id from this closed canon. Choose the most specific id that fits the actual wrong-answer path. Do not invent ids inline. If a genuine, recurring error has no id here, propose an addition and bump the version; this canon is designed upfront so generators never guess. arithmetic_slip is the fallback for a genuine computational slip only, never for a conceptual error. This canon was validated against a v1 pilot, which showed v1 covered only computational errors. Version 2 adds Logical Reasoning misconceptions (blood relations, direction and seating, series and coding) and conceptual or property misconceptions (invariance, relation properties, set operations, definitions).

misconceptions.name: Arithmetic slip
misconceptions.description: A genuine computational slip with sound method. Fallback only.

misconceptions.name: Sign error
misconceptions.description: Dropped or flipped a sign during manipulation.

misconceptions.name: Decimal or power-of-ten error
misconceptions.description: Misplaced a decimal point or a power of ten.

misconceptions.name: Premature or wrong rounding
misconceptions.description: Rounded too early or to the wrong precision, changing the answer.

misconceptions.name: Order of operations
misconceptions.description: Applied operations in the wrong order.

misconceptions.name: Formula misapplied
misconceptions.description: Used a valid formula in a situation it does not cover.

misconceptions.name: Wrong formula chosen
misconceptions.description: Selected the wrong formula for the quantity asked.

misconceptions.name: Unit confusion
misconceptions.description: Mismatched or ignored units (rate per period, currency, time).

misconceptions.name: Percentage base confusion
misconceptions.description: Took the percentage of the wrong base quantity.

misconceptions.name: Ratio inverted
misconceptions.description: Inverted or misordered the terms of a ratio.

misconceptions.name: Simple vs compound interest
misconceptions.description: Applied compound interest where simple was asked, or the reverse.

misconceptions.name: Time period misread
misconceptions.description: Dropped or misread the time period or number of periods.

misconceptions.name: Rate and period mismatch
misconceptions.description: Did not match the interest rate to the compounding period.

misconceptions.name: Inequality sign not flipped
misconceptions.description: Did not reverse the inequality when multiplying or dividing by a negative.

misconceptions.name: Extraneous root kept
misconceptions.description: Kept a root the problem context excludes.

misconceptions.name: Permutation vs combination
misconceptions.description: Counted order where it does not matter, or the reverse.

misconceptions.name: Event vs complement
misconceptions.description: Confused an event with its complement.

misconceptions.name: Independence wrongly assumed
misconceptions.description: Assumed events were independent when they were not.

misconceptions.name: Conditional reversed
misconceptions.description: Computed P(B given A) instead of P(A given B).

misconceptions.name: Mutually exclusive vs independent
misconceptions.description: Confused mutually exclusive events with independent events.

misconceptions.name: Wrong measure of central tendency
misconceptions.description: Used the wrong average for the question.

misconceptions.name: Population vs sample
misconceptions.description: Confused a population parameter with a sample statistic (for example the divisor n vs n-1).

misconceptions.name: Solved the wrong quantity
misconceptions.description: Solved for a different quantity than the one asked.

misconceptions.name: Off by one
misconceptions.description: Off-by-one in counting, indexing, or number of periods.

misconceptions.name: Kinship generation error
misconceptions.description: Placed a family relation at the wrong generational distance, for example uncle vs grandfather or cousin vs sibling.

misconceptions.name: Kinship direction inverted
misconceptions.description: Reversed an ancestor or descendant relation, or took the relation from the wrong person's viewpoint.

misconceptions.name: Kinship gender error
misconceptions.description: Assigned the wrong gender to a relation, giving the wrong gendered term.

misconceptions.name: Direction turn error
misconceptions.description: Turned the wrong way, left for right or the wrong sense of clockwise, at a step of a route or arrangement.

misconceptions.name: Net displacement error
misconceptions.description: Combined the legs of a route incorrectly, giving the wrong final position, distance, or heading.

misconceptions.name: Constraint omitted
misconceptions.description: Reached an answer without applying one or more stated clues or constraints of the puzzle.

misconceptions.name: Constraint reversed
misconceptions.description: Applied a directional or ordering clue backwards, for example read left-of as right-of.

misconceptions.name: Series pattern misidentified
misconceptions.description: Inferred the wrong generative rule for a number or letter series, for example linear growth instead of geometric.

misconceptions.name: Coding rule misapplied
misconceptions.description: Used the wrong shift or mapping when encoding or decoding, or applied it in the wrong direction.

misconceptions.name: Invariance property confused
misconceptions.description: Wrong belief about whether a transformation changes a statistic, for example thinking an origin shift changes a quantity that only a scale change affects.

misconceptions.name: Relation property misidentified
misconceptions.description: Misjudged which of reflexive, symmetric, transitive, or equivalence holds for a relation, by not testing it against a case.

misconceptions.name: Set operation confused
misconceptions.description: Swapped union and intersection, or AND and OR, in a set or probability statement.

misconceptions.name: Concept definition confused
misconceptions.description: Chose an answer reflecting a swapped or confused definition of the concept asked, for example which named index measures what, or which measure is which.
